post.text:
3. Prompt the details to reinforce the guidance
The reference video lacks animation details such as the movement of clothing or hair; prompt these instructions so they appear in the final video.

Seedance 2.0 has high prompt adherence, and even if you have uploaded images and a video, it still gives significant weight to text guidelines.

Additionally, describing what happens in the final scene helps the final generation stay coherent. 

If you don't provide instructions, Seedance 2.0 will tend to simply color your mannequin instead of creating a complete animated scene with clothes, hair, background elements, particles, effects, etc.

Prompt Vídeo 1: Create a an animation based on "Video1" but with the character of"Image1" and the artistic style and background of "Image2"

Prompt Vídeo 2: Create a an animation based on "Video1"but with the character of "Image1". Take poses from "Video1"but add animations of hair and clothes that are not in the original video. Style japanese high budget anime series, $100 million dollar budget

Prompt Vídeo 3: "Video1" = framing, composition and movement . "Image1" = character. "Image2" = background. "Image3" = first frame
The character of "Image1" falls down a vertical tunnel shaft with his hair and clothes moving because of the air. His loose pants ripple and flutter in the rushing air. His oversized upper clothing flaps wildly as he falls. The backpack sways slightly with the motion, while the loose fabric on his back streams and whips violently behind him. Preserve character consitency with "Image1"

Prompt Vídeo 4: Create a an animation based on "Video1" but with the character of "Image1". Take poses from "Video1" but add animations of hair and clothes that are not in the original video. Add moving background visual FX and animations, smeared background in handrawn sketched pencil style. "Image1"is the first frame. Style japanese high budget anime series, 100$ million dollar budget

1. Basic video sketch reference
You might be a traditional animator working on a 2D animation, or a 3D animator with a basic blockout from Blender or other 3D software.

You can use AI to get an idea of what the final look will be, or simply let the AI handle all the detailing and final look while you manually guide the composition and movement.

2. Reference images
You will provide Seedance with a character reference image and a background image so it can generate the final animation. 

You can also create a full-color first frame with the same composition as the first frame of the video; this way, Seedance will carry the character and background throughout the rest of the video frames.

Yes, it will reproduce the animatic but, 

important!!! 

Every line of the sketch seedance will try to draw an element or detail from it. 

If you make animatics specifically for AI try to use models with plain figures and erase first the joints of the sketch.

It can add secondary animations for clothes and hair, with minimal movement.

It works better for wide shots than for medium shots.
